pr_body:
This PR extends the basic Prevalidation API so that in case there are red non-searchable-snapshot indices in the cluster, we reach out to the nodes (whose removal is being prevalidated) to find out if they have a local copy of any red indices.

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/87776
pr_comments: My other question is regarding custom data paths which I think is defined per index using `INDEX_DATA_PATH_SETTING`. I guess since it is deprecated, we do not need to support that here? i.e. looking up the local shard data doesn't have to consider `INDEX_DATA_PATH_SETTING`. Is that correct?

I discussed these questions with @henningandersen and:

> Does sending the list of red shards to the nodes and checking ShardPath and opening it, enough to respond that the node does contain the shard data?

There is no need to try and open the shard. As long as we make sure the path exists, for now that should be considered as "there is some copy of that shard on the node".

> My other question is regarding custom data paths which I think is defined per index using INDEX_DATA_PATH_SETTING.

Since this API could potentially be used by ECE and ECK as well, we should support custom data path setting.

Also a potential refinement for later (I'll put this in an issue at least once part 1 is merged) is to be able to call the Prevalidation API but in case the response is `NO`, up to the `timeout` parameter, internally the API considers reaching out to the nodes again and checking if there has been a change. This could avoid transient `NO`s.
Hi @pxsalehi, I've created a changelog YAML for you.
@henningandersen, this is now ready for review. Please have a look whenever you have time. Thanks!
@henningandersen thank you for the feedback. All comments are addressed in https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/commit/97e25964c5ba9968038f1ec8df59f3a737719283.

issue_context.title: Pre-validate removal of nodes
issue_context.body:
### Description

When a cluster has RED health, a shard is not assigned to a node containing an in-sync copy of the data. If a node is to be removed from the cluster, there is a risk that the last remaining copy of such a shard is on that node. For that reason, orchestration systems typically do not proceed with changes involving node removals to the cluster while it is in RED state.

We propose to add an explicit API `_internal/pre_validate_node_remove` that should be used instead. It can be passed a list of node names/external-ids to remove from the cluster and will give a response per node on whether it is safe as well as a an overall response on the safety of removing all the nodes mentioned.

This check should at least disregard searchable snapshot shards when determining whether it is safe to remove a node. It could also try to reach out to the node to see if the node contains a copy of a RED shard on disk. If it can successfully conclude that it has no copies of RED shards on disk, it can conclude that it is safe to remove the node.

We can also check if any of the nodes not listed in the API has an in-sync copy of such shards. If a node to remove contains a copy but another node contains an in-sync copy for a RED shard, we should indicate it specifically in the response.

Such an API will allow orchestrators to continue with changes to the cluster in many more situations, requiring less manual intervention.

review_comments: I wonder if we risk the shard being allocated back and if we should index a doc into it after relocating the shard in order to prevent it?

Yeah. Although as I was trying to find a way to "leave a stale copy behind", for another test, my understanding was that after the relocation, we always delete the copy on the source node. But to enforce the assumption of the test, I'll add that. Thanks!

Correct, we normally do that - but first of all it is async, so there could be a timing issue. But secondarily, in this test case you simulate failures in the `ACTION_SHARD_EXISTS` action, which I think will prevent removing the shard on disk.

But change looks good, thanks.

Can we also validate that the right nodes are returned? I.e., something like:

```
assertThat(nodeResponses.stream().map(BaseNodeResponse::getNode).map(DiscoveryNode::getId).collect(Collectors.toSet()), equalTo(Set.of(node1Id, node2Id)));
```
